provenance.author: Vincent Russo
provenance.method: exact census of the four-qubit stabilizer states inside the Galois-forced subspace V4: three states, of rank 3, so no four terms

compute.hardware: Apple silicon laptop (shared, load 70), three census runs of 25 s each at m = 4 and 5

llm.role: found the forced-subspace reduction, wrote the census and the certificate

notes: Galois-forced subspace: by cert_sqrtt_galois.py the span of any exact decomposition of |sqrtT>^m contains the four conjugates t_k = (1, zeta^k)^m, k = 1, 5, 9, 13, independent for m >= 3 (their span is V4), and the target lies in V4. Four terms would have to lie inside V4. The certificate enumerates all 36,720 four-qubit stabilizer states exactly from the verifier's parametrization (count and distinctness checked), computes each residue modulo V4 modulo two primes congruent to 1 mod 16 (zeta mapped to a primitive sixteenth root of unity, a ring homomorphism on Z[zeta]), finds exactly three states in the zero set, taken as the union over the two primes of the states whose residue vanishes mod P (|0000> + i|1111>, the uniform odd-weight state, the odd-weight state with sign -1 on weight 3; the same three follow by hand from f(4) = i f(0) on even weights), and their exact rank over Q(zeta_16) is 3. Every step is exact: integer modular arithmetic for the screen and DomainMatrix ranks in Q(zeta_16) for the decisions, no floating-point margin anywhere. With qubit_sqrtT-m4-upper-5.json the cell is exact, chi(|sqrtT>^4) = 5, gamma 0.5805. Controls in the script: at m = 3 the states inside V4 span it (the known rank 4), and the rank-5 census at m = 4 recovers the five product states of the filed witness in one residue class. About 25 s on a laptop.
